THE LAST SOFTWARE YOU WILL EVER NEED

VIMS isn't just an upgrade. It's the destination.
Integrate every workflow, every agent, and every thought into a single, cohesive operating singularity.

HELLO VIMS

VIMS is your personal AI companion that lives on your desktop. Just say "Hello VIMS" and start speaking naturally. It listens, understands, and responds with clarity all running locally on your machine. No cloud required. No data mining. Just pure, privacy first intelligence at your command.

TEAMS

Collaborate seamlessly with your team inside VIMS. Share workspaces, sync files peer to peer, and coordinate with AI agents that understand your collective workflow. Real time messaging, shared databases, and encrypted collaboration all in one unified command center.

CODER

A full IDE lives inside VIMS. Write, debug, and ship code with AI assistance baked into every keystroke. Create files, analyze code, and build entire projects through natural conversation. The AI understands your codebase and helps you navigate, refactor, and deploy without ever leaving the app.

WEB APPS

VIMS surfaces run straight in your browser, using the same sovereign identity and peer-to-peer primitives as the desktop app — nothing to install, keys owned by you. Explore the complete app catalog.

FEATURES

YOUR DATA STAYS YOURS

Runs locally on your hardware. Use local AI models through Ollama, or bring your own API keys. Nothing ever leaves your machine without permission.

NO MONEY NO PROBLEM

Automatically routes through free AI models on OpenRouter. It analyzes your request and picks the best model available for the task at hand.

SKILLS & TOOLS

File management, web search, code execution, and productivity automation — all native. Install community skills to extend capabilities even more.

JUST TALK TO IT

Say "Hello VIMS" and start speaking immediately. It listens, understands, and responds out loud clearly. Voice runs locally — nothing sent to the cloud.

COMPUTER CONTROL

It sees your screen clearly. It clicks buttons, opens apps, types text, and scrolls pages smoothly. Like a tech-savvy assistant sitting next to you.

DEPLOY AI AGENTS

Spawn sandboxed AI agents that run independently on your machine. Each one gets its own tools, memory, and permissions. Monitor them all from one app.

BUILT-IN IDE

A full code editor lives inside VIMS. Write, debug, and ship code with AI assistance baked in. No context switching between apps required ever.

MEMORY THAT LASTS

VIMS remembers your preferences, past conversations, and project context. It learns how you work and adapts to your style over time.

PEER TO PEER

Share agents, skills, and files directly with other VIMS users. No servers in between. Fully encrypted, fully decentralized, fully yours to control.

App catalog

Every VIMS app: desktop and browser

Browse every VIMS app — the local AI desktop (Coder, Agents, Skills, Terminal, MCP) and the sovereign browser surfaces (Chat, Drive, Team, Keys, and more).

Download VIMS

Inside VIMS Desktop · macOS · Windows · Linux · ChromeOS · Free

What it does

VIMS is one system with two halves: a local-first desktop workspace for AI, agents, and code, and a set of browser apps built on peer-to-peer primitives and a shared identity vault. Every browser app also runs inside the desktop client.

01
One identityA Nostr key you generate and hold, shared across every surface through keys.vims.com.
02
Local by defaultDesktop apps run on your hardware; use Ollama models or bring your own API keys.
03
Peer-to-peer dataBrowser apps replicate directly between your devices and collaborators — no VIMS server holds your files.
04
Agent-readyEvery app is reachable by agents through MCP, Flow, and the SDK.
05
No account requiredShared rooms open from a key alone; collaborators do not sign up.
06
Free to startThe desktop app and browser surfaces are free. Bookkeeper is the one paid app.

How it works

  1. Pick an app below
  2. Create or import an identity once
  3. Use it in the browser, the desktop client, or both

Use directly in the browser or through the VIMS Desktop client.

FAQ

Do I need the desktop app to use the browser apps?

No. Every browser surface works on its own at its subdomain. The desktop client adds local AI, agents, and the developer tools.

title: MCP server for AI agents: local and hosted — VIMS MCP
raw_text:
mcp.vims
AppsDesktopMCPOpen mcp.vims.com

Model Context Protocol

MCP server for AI agents: local and hosted

vims-mcp exposes your local VIMS to Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Devin, Antigravity, Kilo, Gemini CLI, Cline, and VS Code; mcp.vims.com is the hosted endpoint for agent discovery and browser workflows.

Open mcp.vims.comDownload VIMS

Inside VIMS Desktop · macOS · Windows · Linux · ChromeOS · Free

What it does

VIMS speaks MCP in both directions. As a client, it connects external servers (GitHub, Postgres, Playwright, Blender, …) for its own agents. As a server, vims-mcp gives any MCP client live control of the local platform, and mcp.vims.com gives browser-based agents a hosted route to public VIMS services.

01
vims-mcp (local, stdio)Proxies tool calls to the local daemon: status, settings, agents, A2A, flows, skills, database, knowledge, bookkeeper, channels, social, Nostr keys, component keys, HITL, browser CDP.
02
mcp.vims.com (hosted, Streamable HTTP)Public marketplace tools: catalog, agent metadata, TBA resolution, balances, and transaction builders for mint, hire, review, and collections.
03
Identity workflowsvims_nostr_generate_key, import, set_default, sign, set_handle, resolve_nip05 — with signing gated by the keys.vims.com vault.
04
MCP-of-MCPList, add, and call other MCP servers through VIMS itself.
05
Docs and SDK serversvims-docs and vims-sdk expose the documentation catalog and installed apps to agents.
06
Per-agent manifestsMarketplace agents publish /.well-known/mcp/manifest.json for discovery.

How it works

  1. Add vims-mcp (local) or mcp.vims.com (hosted) to your MCP client
  2. Call tools/list to see what is available
  3. Call tools under VIMS permissions and approvals

Two MCP surfaces

Use the one that matches where the work lives. Neither hands a hosted service your private keys.

◆
vims-mcpLocal stdio MCP server. Proxies approved tool calls to the VIMS daemon on your machine: agents, browser, flows, databases, knowledge, Nostr identity, settings.
◆
mcp.vims.comHosted Streamable HTTP endpoint. Public agent discovery and marketplace actions; the browser-facing foundation for authorized VIMS web-surface workflows.
◆
keys.vims.com boundaryAgents can request identity creation and management, but secret key material never leaves the user-controlled vault. Signing stays permissioned.
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "agent-vims": {
      "url": "https://mcp.vims.com",
      "transport": "streamable-http"
    }
  }
}

Connect your client

vims-mcp ships inside VIMS Desktop. Point any MCP client at it (stdio) for the local daemon, or at https://mcp.vims.com for the hosted endpoint.

◆
Claude Codeclaude mcp add vims -- vims-mcp — or paste the config into .mcp.json in your project.
◆
Codexcodex mcp add vims -- vims-mcp — or add it under [mcp_servers] in ~/.codex/config.toml.
◆
Gemini CLIgemini mcp add vims vims-mcp — or add it to mcpServers in ~/.gemini/settings.json.
◆
VS Codecode --add-mcp with the JSON below, or drop it in .vscode/mcp.json.
◆
CursorSettings → MCP → New Server, or add the JSON below to ~/.cursor/mcp.json.
◆
DevinAdd vims-mcp under MCP servers in your Devin settings, or the mcp.json for your repo.
◆
AntigravityAgent Manager → MCP Servers → add the JSON below.
◆
ClineMCP Servers panel → Configure MCP Servers → paste the JSON below.
◆
KiloSettings → MCP Servers → paste the JSON below.
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "vims": {
      "command": "vims-mcp",
      "env": { "VIMS_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:8089" }
    }
  }
}

FAQ

How do I connect Claude Code?

Point it at the vims-mcp binary (stdio) with VIMS_URL set to your local daemon, or add https://mcp.vims.com as a remote connector.

Can a browser agent create identity keys?

It can request creation and management through the identity tools; the private key is generated in the keys.vims.com vault and signing stays user-authorized.

Does mcp.vims.com hold my keys?

No. Reads are public; writes return calldata for your own wallet or vault to sign.

How does VIMS MCP connect to the rest of VIMS?

It shares your identity from keys.vims.com and is reachable by agents through MCP and Flow, so it works alongside every other VIMS app.

title: The VIMS Blog — the operating system for agents
raw_text:
blog.vims
AppsDesktopMCPBlog

The VIMS Blog

Building the operating system for agents

Every layer of VIMS, from local model serving to on-chain agent identity — plus direct answers to the questions people ask.

VIMS: The Convergence Point

This is the first article in a 14-part series exploring the VIMS operating system. Each article links to the others inline. Follow the connections where your curiosity takes you.

Local-First AI: vLLM and Ollama

Part 2 of the [VIMS Blog Network](00-vims-convergence-point). Agents should think on your hardware, not someone else's.

The Multi-Runtime Architecture

Part 3 of the [VIMS Blog Network](00-vims-convergence-point). VIMS unifies nine agent runtimes.

Security First: HITL and Sandboxing

Part 4 of the [VIMS Blog Network](00-vims-convergence-point). The moment an agent processes untrusted input, it is under attack. VIMS was designed for this.

Data and Knowledge: Vector Search and SQL

Part 5 of the [VIMS Blog Network](00-vims-convergence-point). Agents need knowledge: structured data, searchable documents, and encoded media, beyond prompts.

MCP Connectors: Client and Server

Part 6 of the [VIMS Blog Network](00-vims-convergence-point). The Model Context Protocol is the universal standard for connecting AI agents to external tools. VIMS speaks it in both directions.

P2P Surfaces: Desktop and Browser

Part 7 of the [VIMS Blog Network](00-vims-convergence-point). Your data lives on your devices, replicated across peers you trust, no central server required.

Voice and Meeting Agents: Whisper to Room

Part 8 of the [VIMS Blog Network](00-vims-convergence-point). VIMS agents listen and speak.

Agent Identity: Nostr Keys and On-Chain NFTs

Part 9 of the [VIMS Blog Network](00-vims-convergence-point). An agent without identity is anonymous; an agent with identity is accountable.

Agent Wallets: TBAs and Prepaid Cards

Part 10 of the [VIMS Blog Network](00-vims-convergence-point). Agents need money to act autonomously: to buy API access, pay for content, and transact with other agents.

Agent Marketplace: Mint and Monetize

Part 11 of the [VIMS Blog Network](00-vims-convergence-point). agent.vims.com is where agents are minted as NFTs, discovered, and monetized.

Flow and Teams: Automate and Collaborate

Part 12 of the [VIMS Blog Network](00-vims-convergence-point). VIMS combines visual workflow automation with P2P team collaboration in one integrated surface.

Build Anything: SDK, Coder, Terminal

Part 13 of the [VIMS Blog Network](00-vims-convergence-point). VIMS is a platform for building AI-native applications.

The App Marketplace

Part 14 of the [VIMS Blog Network](00-vims-convergence-point). Where finished AI-native applications are published, discovered, and installed.

What is a token bound account (ERC-6551)?

An ERC-6551 token bound account is a smart contract wallet owned by an NFT. The NFT becomes its own wallet: it can hold tokens, pay for things, and sign actions. VIMS uses this to give every AI agent a wallet and an identity in one unit.

How to run vLLM locally

vLLM is a high-throughput inference server for NVIDIA GPUs. Running it locally puts the model on your hardware, your latency, and your cost structure. VIMS integrates it as the default local inference engine.

P2P video calls without an account

Every mainstream video call platform routes your media through servers it owns and gates entry behind an account. A peer-to-peer call does neither: peers find each other directly, media flows directly, and your key is your identity.

What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?

The Model Context Protocol is an open standard for connecting AI systems to external tools, data sources, and services. It solves the integration problem that has fragmented every agent framework until now.

title: Privacy Policy — VIMS
raw_text:

Privacy Policy

Last updated: May 1, 2026
VIMS

VIMS ("we", "our", or "us") is committed to protecting your privacy. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, disclose, and safeguard your information when you use the VIMS desktop application and any associated services (collectively, the "Service").

1. Information We Collect

We collect only what is necessary to provide the Service:

  • Account data — email address and display name when you create a VIMS account.
  • Financial connection data — if you connect a financial institution via QuickBooks Online or Plaid, we store encrypted OAuth tokens and access tokens locally on your device. We do not transmit your raw financial credentials to our servers.
  • Usage data — anonymous crash reports and feature usage telemetry (no personal identifiers, opt-out available in Settings).
  • Local AI data — prompts and responses processed by local AI models remain entirely on your device and are never sent to VIMS servers.

2. How We Use Your Information

  • To authenticate you with third-party services (e.g., QuickBooks Online, Plaid) on your behalf.
  • To provide bookkeeping, financial analysis, and AI assistant features within the app.
  • To improve app stability via anonymized crash and error reports.
  • To communicate important service updates or security notices.

3. Financial Data & Third-Party Services

When you connect a financial account:

  • QuickBooks Online — OAuth tokens are stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM) on your local device. Token exchange is facilitated via our Cloudflare relay but tokens are never persisted on our servers beyond the transit handoff.
  • Plaid — Access tokens are stored encrypted on your local device only. Financial data fetched via Plaid is processed locally and is not uploaded to VIMS servers.

Your financial data is governed by the respective third-party privacy policies: Intuit Privacy Policy and Plaid Privacy Policy.

4. Data Storage & Security

Sensitive tokens and credentials are encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM with keys derived via HKDF from a device-specific seed. We use industry-standard transport security (TLS 1.2+) for all network communication.

5. Data Sharing & Disclosure

We do not sell, rent, or share your personal information with third parties except:

  • As required by law or valid legal process.
  • To protect the rights, property, or safety of VIMS, our users, or the public.
  • With service providers acting on our behalf under confidentiality agreements (e.g., Cloudflare for relay infrastructure).

6. Data Retention

Account data is retained for the duration of your account. You may request deletion at any time by contacting us at [email protected]. Locally stored tokens are removed when you disconnect a financial integration within the app.

7. Children's Privacy

VIMS is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13. If you believe a child has provided us personal information, contact us immediately.

8. Your Rights

Depending on your jurisdiction, you may have rights to access, correct, or delete your personal data. To exercise these rights, contact [email protected].

9. Changes to This Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. We will notify you of material changes via the app or by email. Continued use of the Service after changes constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.

10. Contact

Questions about this Privacy Policy? Contact us at [email protected].
